agent_notes: Session-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted after only 9 of the planned ~25 queries could run (a shared cap across this environment, not this unit's own budget) — Tier 1 fully completed, Tier 2/3 mostly blocked, so coverage of social/video/image channels is thin and should be re-run separately. Best find: a Hindi Wikipedia user page (सदस्य:धतरवाल जाट) giving an origin story naming Kolana's founder (Kolaram, son of Kaluram) and dating its vacating to 1981-1986, alongside 11 sibling villages founded by the same lineage (Nathudada) — several of those sibling names (Kheenyera, Soolera, Bheekhnera, Meghana, Thoiya, Manera) match this unit's own 'nearby' list and a Patrika article's list of displaced villages, which cross-corroborates the cluster. Kolana does NOT appear in the current Census2011 Lunkaransar tehsil village list, consistent with it having been vacated/depopulated for the firing range and no longer existing as an inhabited revenue village. Spelling caution: 'Kolayat' (a Bikaner tehsil/town with a sacred lake, unrelated) and 'Kolana, Pipalda tehsil, Kota district' / 'Chetan Patel Kolana' (a different person/place in Kota) are false-positive traps that surface heavily on plain 'Kolana Bikaner' searches — both ruled out and logged below as excluded. jatland.com pages for both 'Kolana' and 'Mahajan' returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch and could not be read; a human researcher with a browser should check both directly. No dedicated news, video, social-media, or image source naming Kolana by name was found in the searches that did run.
